newsitem.title: UK: Vodafone sees subscriber growth slowing.
newsitem.headline: Vodafone sees subscriber growth slowing.

text.p: British mobile phone operator Vodafone Group Plc said on Tuesday it expected to win 350,000 to 400,000 net new subscribers in Britain, its biggest market, in the current financial year.
Chief executive Chris Gent told Reuters in an interview that he expected growth at a slightly lower level than the previous year.
"I suspect this year will be similar to last year...perhaps a little bit down but not much," he said.

Gent, who expected the company's booming overseas operations to see a 650,000 rise in subscribers in the current year, said the company would focus on reducing churn -- the numbers of subscribers who end their contracts -- in order to raise penetration levels.
Last year, subscribers in Britain rose by 415,000 customers, a 34 percent decline in growth from the previous year.
He said he expected growth in Britain to accelerate once penetration reached the 15 percent level from 13 percent at present.
Gent said that target could possibly be reached next year.
In order to increase penetration to Scandinavian levels of 30 to 40 percent -- expected in around 10 years -- Gent said Vodafone planned a complete rethink of its distribution strategy.
The company, which currently has 12 brands, is considering pulling the various tradenames under one or two brands as well as introducing a unified billing system, Gent said.
Gent said key overseas operations all performed better than expected, with its troubled Australian businesses increasing growth every month this year.
Gent said the Australian business, which has over 300,000 subscribers, needs 460,000 to break even.
"We are nine months away from break-even," he said.
Vodafone said it was reasonably confident that the German business would break even in the back end of 1998, slightly behind schedule.
Vodafone has a 17.2 percent stake in the country's third-largest cellular operator, E-Plus Mobilfunk.
